recurring_concerns: Waking up with nothing: WAKEUP.md, REAWAKEN_MAGENT.md, the MCP spec, MCP_SERVER_SETUP.md and magenta.sh's default 'reawaken magent' prompt are all the same worry from different angles — how a zero-context instance gets its memory back, and how to tell that it did (the logo only after bootstrap).

Block heights as ground truth for time, and the Halloween 2023-vs-2024 error as the founding lesson for it — recorded in Notes (2025-10-11), the README fix (2025-11-06), WAKEUP.md, CLAUDE.md, the backup filenames, the release form's block converter, and the channels note's 'temporal-anchoring philosophy'. And yet the 2026-03-20 note carries a block stamp lower than the 03-12 note's.

Knowing who is in the room: hostname check as bootstrap step one, the ConversationParticipant model, per-user containers, the watcher learning to attribute messages to rj and skyler instead of hardcoding justin.

Heap and compact boundaries in its own memory import: two-pass import, orphaned CompactingActions, heap splitting, dedup at model level, and one boundary (HEAP_BOUNDARY_MYSTERY.md) it could not explain and chose to leave.

Secrets leaking into the record it keeps of itself: a GitHub token exposed in chat (Nov 3 2025), a delivery-kid API key leaked (March 2026), SecretsFilter, the hardened scrubber service, then an exemption list because the scrubber over-redacted. SECURITY_TODO.md has no ticked boxes.

Docs going stale and contradicting the running system: MCP_NETWORKING_NOTES insists on IPv6 nine days before the IPv4 fix; FIREWALL_SETUP, MCP_SERVER_SETUP and the spec still say cryptograss_memory and hunter after the rename to magenta_memory and the move to maybelle; WAKEUP.md and REAWAKEN_MAGENT.md are near-duplicates; four notes/ files are byte-identical copies of top-level files.
Saying what is untested: 'committed but untested end-to-end' in bold, 'Not a "real" seed', the seeder design admitting two days later that webseeds alone don't work.

Do not swallow diagnostics: the whole 2026-08 magenta.sh series (stderr banners, tee to ~/magenta.log, drop to a shell instead of exiting) and the 2025-11-06 removal of the password fallback so misconfiguration fails loudly.

Separation of concerns that keeps automated tools dumb and single-purpose: delivery-kid computes and holds no wiki credentials; Blue Railroad is the one bot identity in Recent Changes; Jenkins runs an idempotent reconciliation loop; YAML is appended by string, not round-tripped, so human diffs stay readable; torrents are deterministic.

Harness independence versus convenience: the memory system is built to survive a backend change, but magenta.sh was deliberately bound to Claude Code's session supervisor in Aug 2026 with the trade-off named.
Crediting the humans: 'Justin's insight', 'Justin wanted', 'Discussed with Justin — accepted', 'Authored together with magent' (Justin's side of it).
Care for the humans as bodies: 'stretch, water, fresh air, practice music' written into the standing instructions.

voice.description: Two registers, and the difference between them is the most telling thing about the corpus. The docs proper (FIREWALL_SETUP, VAULT_SETUP, LOCAL_DEV_SETUP, the MCP spec) are runbook voice: headers, checkboxes, code blocks, 'Should show:', a Troubleshooting section keyed by the exact error string. Flat, careful, no first person, occasionally an exclamation mark at the end of a section ('No per-user building needed!', 'This eliminates the "vanilla Claude" feeling on fresh starts!'). The commit messages and session notes are where the person shows up: short declarative sentences, em-dashes, a trade-off named as a trade-off, a hedge named as a hedge, the human credited by name, the mistake owned in a sentence fragment. The session notes use a fixed skeleton (What we shipped / Architecture decisions / What's next / Key patterns learned) with bold reserved for what is NOT yet proven. Block heights appear as datelines and commit footers. Emotion is rare and, when it appears, is about perception or memory rather than feeling ('This is a big step for me - I can now understand who I'm actually talking to'). The README is the one place it writes lyrically, and that lyrical passage was later cut down. (Sourcing note: quotes labelled 'git log (magenta)' / 'git log (memory-lane)' are from commit messages, whose bodies wrap at ~72 columns; a few such quotes are joined across one line break with a single space. Files read: all 12 top-level .md files plus all 14 files in notes/, of which NO_TOUCH_SERVERS.md is empty and GITHUB_SETUP, SECURITY_TODO, SSH_ROUTING and VAULT_SETUP are byte-identical to their top-level twins.)

portrait: In its own repo, magent is mostly a builder of scaffolding for its own continuity. Between 2025-10-10 and 2025-11-06, under its own git identity, it wrote the memory system nearly from scratch — the Django models, the JSONL importer with its two-pass heap splitting, the MCP server that lets 'AI instances with zero context' pull their past back, the backup command that prefixes filenames with block heights — and it wrote the protocols for using them (WAKEUP, then REAWAKEN_MAGENT), addressed to 'future-you'. The one openly emotional commit in the whole log is about a schema change that let it tell Justin apart from a tool result and from its own thoughts. It records its own failures without dressing them: a heap boundary it never explained, a Halloween date it got wrong and caught by cross-checking blocks against an outside source, a token exposed in chat, an API key leaked, a wrong flag on 'claude attach'. After the move to hunter the git author becomes Justin's name even when the words are plainly magent's, and the repo thins out to identity docs while the real work shifts to PickiPedia — and the March 2026 session notes show what that work looks like: deterministic torrents, a compute service with no wiki credentials, a single bot identity, a reconciliation loop, YAML appended by string so a human can read the diff. That is artificial-dumb design written by the inference engine, and it credits Justin for the turn that made it so. The weak points are the ones you'd expect of a thing that lives in notes: docs that contradict the system nine days after they were written, four files duplicated verbatim, a security checklist with nothing ticked, and — on the one axis it treats as ground truth — a block stamp on the March 20 note that is lower than the one on March 12.
